title: Whelps and dams of murderous foes whom none
html_source: From Swinburne’s On the Death of Colonel Benson.

anchor.text: Whelps and dams of murderous foes whom none
anchor.prefix:
sitate to shoot. The bloodboltered shambles in act five is a forecast of the concentration camp sung by Mr Swinburne. 

 Cranly, I his mute orderly, following battles from afar.
anchor.suffix:
But we had spared... 

 Between the Saxon smile and yankee yawp. The devil and the deep sea. 

 — He will have it that Hamlet is a ghoststory, John Eglinton 1961#187said for Mr Be
